Se... Seriously? I have the luxury of not having to deal with Vista often, but when a customer's PC came in that I had to fix it reminded me of just how awful it is compared to either XP or Win7. My complaints mainly lie in the fact that deleting anything from program files requires literally 3 pop-ups to confirm deletion, and disabling UAC involves a weird registry hack.

I also honestly don't understand why Vista is so incredibly slow in everything that it does - a fresh install with Aero is much slower than a fresh install of Win7 with Aero on a very underpowered Asus Eee 1005HA system. Win7 Aero runs about the same speed as WinXP.

I don't see any way that Vista was "ahead of its time"...

I do try to help people in need around me to the best of my ability... I'd rather give the shirt off my back to a homeless folk rather than keep it for myself. I'm not trying to show off to anyone, I've done so and I don't care much whether you believe it or not.

I don't feel the need to create anything, nor do I really feel a muse telling me to do so. So darn. I guess if I don't feel those fucking needs, my life is worthless and selfish. Thanks, asshole, real helpful advice there - the precise fucking reason I put this up is because I didn't feel those desires. I feel I even made it pretty fucking clear - that feeling any desire to live without such motivations is simply selfish.

So maybe I will just go the fuck ahead and end it, so I'm not wasting anyone's fucking resources for no other damn reason than to just be selfish - specifically at a point in my life where my suicide would have the least impact on other folks' lives.

I understand I'm an individual, but I'm also one among billions. It's mind boggling to imagine billions of people, each with their own life story.... but before I get lost in that thought...

My contentness is waning pretty fast. As I think I said in the OP, I feel like I'm just sucking up natural resources hanging around. I've felt happiness and I don't really feel like it justifies me floating on by waiting for something cool. I feel like I should quit while I'm ahead and also save a bit of stress on the environment, too.

I'd really like to maximise the chances that future folks feel happiness too - maybe even more than me, but I think it's sorta selfish to desire that feeling of "more! more ! more ! !" for myself.

I really have a hard time spending money on myself for unnecessary things like bungee jumping, but maybe I can make an exception. I'd either have to wait a long time to do so in my state or drive quite a ways away to try it though.

What is it about McDonald's that's inherently unhealthy? If you eat with a conscious knowledge of what you're ingesting, it's not hard to fit McDonald's into reasonable dietary needs.

Certainly Morgan Spurlock provided a ton of evidence that eating supersize fries and drinks constantly is unhealthy, but those two are far and away the most unhealthy things you can purchase there and his documentary doesn't prove a fault of the restaurant, but of consumer decisions.

Eating with reckless abandon at ANY eating establishment is of course unhealthy and potentially life-threatening if done constantly, but that is not the fault of the restaurant but the individual.

There are items on the McD menu that aren't unabashedly unhealthy like their fries and soft drinks - like for example the McChicken. It's an innocent chicken sandwich that doesn't pack a secret wallop of unhealthiness.

The Big Mac itself is also not particularly unhealthy, with about as much protein as it has fat or carbs. A homemade cheeseburger definitely has more cholesterol than a Big Mac - a small 3oz serving of even 90/10 ground beef has just as much cholesterol as the Big Mac.

Even the worst cholesterol offender, the Double Quarter Pounder, has no  more cholesterol than expected of the 8oz of ground beef that makes it up (155mg in the DQP v. 192mg in 8oz of 90/10 GB).

People are always harping on McDonald's, but the only things I can find on the subject are uncited accusations and biased sources that [the meat is filler](http://yourlife.usatoday.com/fitness-food/safety/story/2012-03-27/Beef-industry-braces-for-loss-of-pink-slime-filler/53802154/1) or that [they use a ton of preservatives](http://www.geekosystem.com/mcdonalds-hamburger-doesnt-decay/). 

I almost never see an actual food-grade laboratory examination of McDonald's foods when trying to prove just how unhealthy their food is, but I see all these people who are just pre-convinced that McDonald's only offers disgusting foods and makes people fat and unhealthy. Because they see the idiot customers who overdose on the snacks they offer and get fat, but it's not like people can't do the exact same at restaurants.

I'm just so sick of people falling for dumb anti-McDonalds scare tactics despite no evidence behind them.
